hard_case: the `.then` carries a rejection handler, so rule 2 collects nothing, yet the handler only catches a rejection of `orderSum` and the failing assertion still rejects the returned promise

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the sum starts at 1, so `orderSum([10, 20])` resolves to 31 instead of 30

reasoning: `items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item, 0)` becomes `..., 1)`. The test returns `orderSum([10, 20]).then((sum) => { expect(sum).toBe(30); }, () => {})`; the rejection handler only handles a rejection of `orderSum`, so the failing `expect` in the fulfilment handler rejects the returned promise and jest fails the test on 31. RIPR-SPEC-0246 example 7: a `.then` with a rejection handler collects no assertion. ripr reads no oracle in the test (`unknown`) and reports `weakly_exposed`, as the spec states; against the discriminated truth that is a false actionable gap the spec accepts.
